idiom_name: Kysely type-safe query builder over a Database interface
implementation_notes: The query object is a builder whose types are derived from a Database schema interface: Kysely checks at compile time that tables and columns exist in the scope where they are referenced, returns a new builder from every clause (where/leftJoin/orderBy/limit) and infers the result row type including aliases; rendering to SQL with bound parameters happens when the builder is executed against a dialect (pg, mysql2, sqlite). What replaces the classic query class is the type-level schema plus the fluent builder, with sql`` template tags as the escape hatch; a hand-written query class is justified only when a query must be serialised or validated independently of a dialect.
pitfalls: The Database interface is compile-time only: a migration that renames a column breaks at runtime unless the interface is regenerated from the schema.
Conditional clauses ($if) are typed as the full builder, so a clause referencing a not-yet-joined column fails to compile or needs a cast.
Builders are immutable: dropping the returned builder loses the clause, and mixing raw sql`` fragments with the typed builder reintroduces unbound text.
